newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: American Airlines drops Zurich-New York route.
newsitem.headline: American Airlines drops Zurich-New York route.

text.p: American Airlines, a unit of AMR Corp, has decided to stop flying directly between Zurich and New York from February 1, a spokesman for the airline said.
The spokeswoman, who confirmed an article in the Swiss daily newspaper Tages-Anzeiger, said the costs of flying the route was the main reason for the decision.
The decision means that Swissair AG is the only airline to fly non-stop from Zurich to New York, a Swissair spokesman said.
Swissair has three daily flights to the New York area: one from Zurich to John F. Kennedy (JFK) airport, one from Zurich to Newark and one from Geneva to JFK.
American Airlines will continue its daily service between Zurich and Chicago, the spokeswoman added.
Quoting Antony Levenberg, sales manager for American Airlines in Zurich, the Tages-Anzeiger said the decision was not based on the fares charged for the route, but rather costs.
A average load factor of 70-75 percent was described by Levenberg as "very acceptable."
However, the cost of using Zurich and New York's JFK airports are very high. This applies to landing fees, maintenance, check-in services and wages.
American Airlines has been losing money on the Zurich-New York route for years, the newspaper added.
